The board

M2e Choices mock-up, 2026-11-17. The board isn't built yet. These are screenshots of today's game on seed 1 at real hour 4 (tick 960, the soak's scripted player: 15 residents, a Woodcutter's camp, Forager's hut, Mine, Workshop and two Cottages), with the board drawn into the page in the game's own styles. Its numbers come from the approved spec's rules on the stock each screenshot shows.

The board sits on the Town tab under the Hall, above the work queue. It holds goals, the trader's offers, goods on the way and a forage trip. Nothing on it runs out while you are away, and nothing needs a tap to collect.

1. A check-in

What you see

Two goals to pick from, two swaps waiting, and the trip. Each goal shows roughly what it would pay into the stores right now. Accept is amber because the town has the 40 wood.

The same at 360 px, the narrow width. Nothing scrolls sideways.

2. After choosing

Picked a goal, took a swap, sent a trip

"A good harvest" now shows its progress and the other goal says Pick instead. The 40 wood left at once (wood 186 to 146); 13 tools arrive a game day later. Llew and Ceria are at the forest edge for a game day. With less wood in the stores, the "Worth about" lines now put more of the reward into wood.

Measured on the same town without the board: it makes 61 food in the next half real hour and 123 in the next real hour, so this goal would be met within about an hour.

3. Short of wood

Swaps you can't pay right now

The same check-in if the town had spent its wood on building and had 30 left (set by hand to show the state). Both swaps ask for 40 wood, so Accept is outlined and the line under it says what is missing, as the Upgrade row does. The offers stay until they leave, so you can take one once the wood is back. With room for 80 more wood, "Lay in timber" can be offered again, so three goals show.

When every goal for the Hall's tier is done or can't fit the stores, the goals card reads "No goals until the town grows".

4. Choosing who goes

The trip sheet

Send two opens a sheet with everyone who is not already on a trip. Residents with no work are listed first, then everyone by name, so the ones the town can spare are at the top. Tap a row to tick it; Send works at exactly two.

5. People: pins and trips

Pinned label and filter; On a trip

A pinned resident gets a "Pinned" label by the name instead of " · Pinned" at the end of the line, and a Pinned chip shows only them. A resident on a trip reads "On a trip" in place of a trade and is not counted as having no work.

Things to look at

Only two goals by real hour 4

The spec offers three goals, but a goal that is already true can't be offered, and a make goal can't be offered if the stores couldn't hold it. On this town at real hour 4, Open the quarry, Light the forge and Twelve hearths are already done, and Lay in timber doesn't fit (186 of 200 wood). So only two Hamlet goals are left. Recommended: add more Hamlet goals in S1 (for example stone, ore and tools goals), each with a reward of about an hour of work, and measure that three are on offer at every check-in on the soak.

Changes from the spec's wording

  • A trader card is titled with the swap ("50 food for 40 wood") instead of the line "The trader offers 50 food for 40 wood", so the trader's cards stay short.
  • Each card has a small kind label at the top right: Goal, Trader, Delivery, Trip.
  • The trip sheet lists residents with no work first and says anyone with no work may take the jobs of the two who go.
  • New styles: the kind label, the Pinned label and the sheet's tick rows. All use the existing colours.

If you approve, the spec changes with the mock-up before S1.

Long board

Five cards push the lots about a screen further down. Each card is kept roomy because you asked for a bigger picture on every board card (art round 1); the pictures come with the art steps, not M2e.

"Leaves in 80 game days"

Offers last longer than your longest time away (8 real hours at the Hamlet), which reads as 80 to 90 game days. The style rule says time is shown in game units, so it stays that way unless you say otherwise.
